title: Ordinary colimits assembled over a directed cover of the index category
statement: Fix a universe $\mathcal U$, and call sets and categories small when they belong to it. Let $I$ be a small nonempty poset such that every finite subset has an upper bound. Let $C$ be a small ordinary category and $(C_i)_{i\in I}$ full subcategories, with literal inclusions $C_i\subseteq C_j$ for $i\leq j$, such that every object of $C$ belongs to some $C_i$. A full subcategory contains every morphism of $C$ between its objects. Let $\mathcal A$ be an ordinary category with small Hom sets and all small colimits [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], and let $F:C\to\mathcal A$ be a functor. Choose colimit cocones $(L_i,(\lambda_{i,c})_{c\in C_i})$ for $F|_{C_i}$ and $(L,(\lambda_c)_{c\in C})$ for $F$. For $i\leq j$, let $u_{ij}:L_i\to L_j$ be the unique map satisfying $u_{ij}\lambda_{i,c}=\lambda_{j,c}$ for every $c\in C_i$, and let $v_i:L_i\to L$ be the unique map satisfying $v_i\lambda_{i,c}=\lambda_c$. Then the maps $u_{ij}$ define an $I$-diagram, and $(L,(v_i))$ is a colimit cocone on it. More precisely, for every $H\in\mathcal A$, taking the composites with $\lambda_{i,c}$ gives a bijection between families $f_i:L_i\to H$ satisfying $f_j u_{ij}=f_i$ and cocones $(g_c:F(c)\to H)_{c\in C}$ on $F$; it sends $g_c$ to the unique $f_i$ with $f_i\lambda_{i,c}=g_c$ on $C_i$. The comparison $\operatorname{colim}_{i\in I}L_i\to L$ induced by the $v_i$ is therefore an isomorphism with these specified legs. Empty $C$ and empty members $C_i$ are allowed.
